question: ResetGameStateToStartDate's name; the rest of CGameState_ResetAtHistoryExecute (0x27B240); and the CInGameIdler +0x1790 session_manager / CEU3Application conflict

addresses.name: CGameState_StartupResetAndLoadGameplaySettings
addresses.revises: The body is now read end to end. The old name CGameState_ResetAtHistoryExecute described the one call site, and its own comment said so; the function's last 0x560 bytes build a path and parse gameplaysettings.txt into the state, which the name said nothing about.
addresses.comment:
0x67B240..0x67BAE8 inclusive - the `ret 4` at 0x67BAE6 is three bytes - so 0x8A9 = 2217 bytes, 586 instructions, one `ret 4`, one stack argument. Extent clean of traps 2 and 3: retsBefore(0x67B240, 0x67BB00) returns exactly one ret, and seven int3 separate it from CGameState::ResetSession at 0x67BAF0. **Exactly one caller**, 0x23286D, inside CEU3Application::LoadEverything (0x62FAC0..0x632CE6 by the int3 scan), at the `history execute <` stage; so it runs once per process, at startup, on the global game state, before the first screen exists - the first CFrontEnd is constructed later in the same function, at 0x2329DE.

What it does, in order: (1) 0x27B29E state->+0xF0 = <the 4-byte factory at [0x174DA90], vftable 0x15FDF60>->slot1(), which allocates a 4-byte object with vftable 0x15FDCFC, and then calls slot 1 on that, which is the 1691-holder empty stub 0xABF890. (2) get-or-creates g_CCurrentGameState (dead - it exists from the database stage). (3) 0x27B33B..0x27B3C1 collects every country's tag (CCountry +0xCA4) out of state->countries_begin (+0xBBC) into a local std::vector<Hoi3CString>, hands it to 0x148B0, and passes the 0x10-byte result **by value** to 0x1F3640(state->income_statistics (+0xC6C), keys) - 0x1F3640 ends `ret 0x14`, which is what identifies the second argument as the 0x10-byte temp rather than a discarded local. So the statistics series are re-keyed by country tag. (4) only when state->+0xCEC == 0 (jne at 0x27B406 skips it): rebuilds the singly linked list at state->+0xCE8 with count +0xCEC and tail +0xCE4, one 0x10-byte node {value, next, 0, 0} per element of the vector at +0x1C of the global at [0x1A878BC] whose virtual slot 6 returns true, the value being that element's +0x54 or, when that is null, the CNullFaction singleton at [0x1A855A8] (lazily built with 0x1224B0 and given vftable 0x15C248C). (5) 0x27B58D..0x27B59F clears in_game_screen (+0xBE8), loaded_from_save (+0xD9C), **in_game (+0xDA4)** and tutorial_id (+0xDA0). (6) CGameState_SetProvincesAndSizePerCountryVectors(state, [0x1A8557C]+0x2200). (7) get-or-creates the 0x57C-byte CCountryDataBase at [0x1A855A4] with CCountryDataBase::CCountryDataBase (0x2024D0), then 0x27E550(state, &db->+0x16C), which clears and resizes both state->countries (+0xBBC/+0xBC0) and state->played_countries (+0xBCC) to the database's country count and copies every CCountry* across, zeroing the played entry for each. (8) **CGameState::ResetSession (0x27BAF0)** at 0x27B5F3. (9) 0x28A6E0([0x1A8557C]), which parses `<...>/colors.txt`. (10) 0x27B604..0x27BA69: assigns the string 'gameplaysettings.txt' (the image's only reference to it, 0x15CF29C), and when the mod-name string the settings singleton at [0x1A863F8] yields through 0x40C600 is non-empty, replaces it with 'mod/' + <mod> + '/' + 'gameplaysettings.txt'; then FileExists (0x784A20) on it, and when it exists builds a 0x114-byte tokenizer over the file - an inlined copy of **Tokenizer::Tokenizer (rva 0x669990, VA 0xA69990)**, which project.json already records as 0x114 bytes with vftable 0x11FD1FC (rva) = 0x15FD1FC (VA), the same table written here at 0x27B9AD, with 0xA6C1B0 and 0xA69AD0 as its internals - and an inlined CParseContext (0x360 bytes, vftable 0x15FD93C, name 'UNNAMED_SESSION', tokenizer at +0x1C - the same object CParseContext::CParseContext 0x67A460 builds) and calls **virtual slot 3 of the game state - [0x15CF674+0xC] = 0xA7C050, CPersistent::Load** - on it, then releases it through slot 0 with 1. (11) frees the tag vector.

**So the mod's own `mod/<mod>/gameplaysettings.txt`, if present, is parsed into the game state at startup through CGameState::LoadKey, and when a mod is active the game-root copy is not read at all.** Neither file exists in this install, so the parse is skipped here.

For the DLL: this is the only writer of in_game that is neither a construction nor a screen transition, it runs once, at startup, before any screen exists, and its clear writes 0 over a byte that is already 0. It changes nothing about Gui::Lua::sessionActive() or GameClock::movedInPlay().
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: disasm of 0x67B240..0x67BAE7 (586 instructions), cfg.py 0x67B240 0x8A7 for the branch structure, and --lands-in on 0x67B581, 0x67B892, 0x67BA6B for the edges. Extent: image.retsBefore(0x67B240, 0x67BB00) returns exactly one (0x67BAE6, 'ret 4') and the bytes at 0x67BAE5 are `5d c2 04 00` then seven int3 then `55 8b ec` - neither trap 2 nor trap 3. One caller by findRefs.py --callers 0x67B240; LoadEverything's extent 0x62FAC0..0x632CE6 from an int3-run scan over 0x62F000..0x633000, which also puts the CFrontEnd construction at 0x6329DE inside it and after 0x63286D. Virtual slot 3 read directly out of vftable 0x15CF674: slot 3 = 0xA7C050, which project.json has as CPersistent::Load with 748 holders. CParseContext identified by project.json's own entry for 0x67A460, whose comment gives vftable 0x11FD93C (rva) = 0x15FD93C (VA) and the tokenizer at +0x1C, matching field for field. 0x1F3640's `ret 0x14` from retsBefore is what makes the 0x10-byte by-value second argument legible. 'gameplaysettings.txt' has exactly one reference in .text (image.findValue(0x15CF29C) = [0x67B607]). **What would show it wrong:** a second caller of 0x27B240 reached after a session exists, which findRefs over every `call rel32` denies; or the CParseContext at 0x67B8C3 turning out not to be one, which reading vftable 0x15FD93C's slots against 0x67A460's own writes would settle; or the mod-path gate at 0x67B699 reading something other than a string length, which would make the mod-file claim wrong while leaving the game-root one standing.

addresses.name: ResetGlobalIdCounters
addresses.comment: 0x63A330..0x63A454, bare `ret`, no arguments. Sets **four globals to 1** - [0x170AF7C] at 0x23A35A, [0x170AF78] at 0x23A360, [0x170AEB8] at 0x23A3CF and [0x170AEBC] at 0x23A441 - with two copies of the inlined get-or-create of g_CCurrentGameState between them, both dead (the global is non-null from the database stage on). It does nothing else. Two callers and no others: ResetGameStateToStartDate at 0x23A587 and the savegame loader CGameState::LoadFromSave at 0x27CEAD, i.e. exactly the two places that have just wiped or are about to overwrite the object graph. The four globals have 10, 33, 16 and 20 references; the named functions among their readers are CGameState::LoadKey (two of them), CCreateHigherCommand::Execute, CreateRebelsForFaction and CSubUnit::AfterLoad, which is what the name reads: next-free-id counters, put back to 1. `inferred` - the individual counters were not followed to the point of naming what each one counts.
addresses.evidence: Full body disassembled, 0x63A330..0x63A454; retsBefore(0x63A330, 0x63A730) gives one bare ret at 0x63A454 and five int3 follow. The four stores of 1 are the only writes in it apart from the two dead accessor copies. findRefs.py --callers 0x63A330 is not what attributes the callers here - the two call sites are the ones project.json already records (0x23A587 inside ResetGameStateToStartDate, 0x27CEAD inside CGameState::LoadFromSave). Readers of each global by image.findValue + functionStart. **What would show it wrong:** any of the four globals turning out to be a flag rather than a counter - the test is whether a reader increments it or compares it, and only a sample of the 79 references was looked at, which is why this is `inferred` and not `confirmed`.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::CEU3Application
addresses.revises: The entry is named SessionManager::SessionManager and says 'No RTTI'. Both are wrong: the function writes CEU3Application's own RTTI vftables, and the string `SessionManager` does not occur anywhere in the image.
addresses.comment: The constructor of the object at CInGameIdler +0x1790, CFrontEnd +0x210 and CBackEndIdler +0xB8. At 0x22F134 it writes **[this] = 0x15CD1A8** and at 0x22F13A **[this+8] = 0x15CD1D0**; the RTTI export names those two tables `CEU3Application` (9 slots at offset 0, 4 at +8). retsBefore(0x62F080, 0x62F140) is empty, so both writes are inside this function, and 0x62F070 holds `14 c3` then 14 int3, so 0x62F080 is a real entry. One caller, 0xA59C43, at startup. Body otherwise as recorded: builds 'HoI3 v4.02' and 'HoI3', calls the base constructor 0x6909A0, builds the startup session with mode 2 at 0x22F30F and stores it at [this+0x12C]; `ret 0xC`, returns this in eax. The `SessionManager` reading came from that one field - the application *holds* a session, it is not a session manager - and `MakeBackEndIdler` is a real symbol, so the concept exists in the source without being this class's name. The signature gains an explicit __stdcall and a typed `this`, which is what lets scripts/checkSignatures.py check it: under the old name it was skipped twice, for 'no virtual table recorded for SessionManager' and 'no calling convention in the signature'. Simulated against a patched copy of project.json, the renamed entry is **checked and passes both tests** - `ret 0xC` against three stack arguments, and the constructor-against-vftable test, which can only run once the class name matches an RTTI table.
addresses.evidence: The two vftable writes read in the disassembly at 0x62F134/0x62F13A; retsBefore(0x62F080, 0x62F140) empty, so they are inside the function; the RTTI export (luabindExtract.load_rtti) maps 0x15CD1A8 -> CEU3Application (9 slots) and 0x15CD1D0 -> CEU3Application (4 slots). A byte search over every section for `SessionManager`, `CSessionManager`, `session_manager` and `sessionmanager` returns **zero** hits; the same search finds `CEU3Application` in .data at 0x171796C (the RTTI type descriptor) and `eu3application` in .rdata at 0x15CC508, which is the positive control that the search can see both kinds of name. findRefs.py --callers 0x62F080 gives one caller. **What would show it wrong:** 0x15CD1A8 being held by a second class, which the RTTI map denies; or the write at 0x62F134 belonging to an inlined base constructor rather than this one, which the empty retsBefore and the 14-byte int3 run before 0x62F080 argue against. And the rename is itself machine-checked: run against a patched copy of project.json, checkSignatures.py --only 0x22F080 --verbose goes from 2 skips to '1 entries checked against their ret / none disagree', which means the constructor-against-vftable test ran and agreed - i.e. a machine confirmed that this function writes CEU3Application's own table.

addresses.name: CEU3Application::MakeBackEndIdler
addresses.revises: Only the class qualifier changes. The receiver is the object at CInGameIdler +0x1790, which 0x22F080's vftable writes identify as a CEU3Application, not a SessionManager; `SessionManager` is not a string in the image.
addresses.comment: thiscall on the CEU3Application; the CBackEndIdler is the first stack argument. Writes its own this into [idler+0xB8], the sibling into +0xB4 and arg3 into +0xB0. One caller, 0x254518 in ProcessSessionEndRequests, which loads the receiver with `mov ecx, [ebx+0x1790]` at 0x254510 - and +0x1790 is the application. Calls CGameState::SetInGameScreen (0x280F30) at 0x208925, so on the game-over frame state->in_game_screen is a CBackEndIdler while in_game is still 1. The body description is unchanged; only the qualifier was wrong.
addresses.evidence: Rests entirely on 0x22F080 above plus the receiver load. The one call site, 0x254518, loads ecx from [ebx+0x1790] at 0x254510 - that instruction appears in a per-displacement scan of .text for 0x1790, which finds 32 accesses and exactly one write. **What would show it wrong:** the same thing that would unseat 0x22F080's rename. Nothing about the body changes either way, so this is a qualifier change only and it is reversible at no cost.

struct_fields.name: application
struct_fields.revises: The field is named session_manager, from a reading of its one writer, and its own comment records that the live object resolves by RTTI to a CEU3Application and that the conflict was left unresolved. The static chain below closes it, and the DLL's own source already calls the offset IDLER_APPLICATION.
struct_fields.comment: The CEU3Application. Constructor argument 4, written at 0x248418 - the **only** write to this displacement in the image (a per-displacement scan over .text finds 32 accesses to +0x1790, 31 reads and that one write). The chain, every link in the bytes: CEU3Application::LoadEverything constructs the first CFrontEnd at 0x2329DE with `mov ecx,[edi+0x120]; mov edx,[edi+0x11c]; push edi; push ecx; push edx; push eax; call 0x6ed660`, where edi is the application - its +0x11C and +0x120 are the already-named `graphics` and `gui` - so **arg4 is the application's own `this`**; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg4 at CFrontEnd +0x210 (already recorded); CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler is called once, from CFrontEnd::LaunchGame at 0x2F1144, with [frontEnd+0x20C], [frontEnd+0x60], [frontEnd+0x210] as args 1-3 after `this`, and copies the third to +0x1790. Live RTTI on the object agrees (2026-10-02), as does the DLL: BiceLib/Gui/WidgetStats.cpp already spells this offset `IDLER_APPLICATION`. Its +0x12C is the session, which virtual slot 18 (CInGameIdler::GetSession, 0x24D800) returns and which every CCommand is posted to - that field is where the name `session_manager` came from.
struct_fields.evidence: Three independent routes, two static and one live. Static route A: a per-displacement scan over .text for 0x1790 (decode forward from each plausible start before the displacement bytes, keep the decodes whose own displacement field lands on them) finds 32 accesses, 31 reads and **one** write, at 0x648418, `mov [ebx+0x1790], edx` with edx = [ebp+0x14]; findRefs.py --callers 0x6474A0 gives CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler exactly one caller, 0x6F1144, whose pushes are [fe+0xC0], mpByte, [fe+0x210], [fe+0x60], [fe+0x20C], this - so +0x1790 = [frontEnd+0x210]. Static route B: CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd's record already says it stores arg4 at +0x210, and its first construction, 0x6329DE in LoadEverything, pushes `edi` as arg4 while reading [edi+0x11C] and [edi+0x120] as args 2 and 3 - and project.json already names CEU3Application +0x11C `graphics` and +0x120 `gui`, so edi is the application. Route C: the live RTTI read recorded on the field itself, and BiceLib/Gui/WidgetStats.cpp:81-86, which names the offset IDLER_APPLICATION and documents the same walk. **What would show it wrong:** edi at 0x6329CE not being the application - the discriminator is the +0x11C/+0x120 pair, which is trap 12 territory on its own, so the check is that CEU3Application::CEU3Application (0x22F080) writes the CEU3Application vftable into the same object the single caller 0xA59C43 passes; or a second writer of +0x1790 that the displacement scan missed, whose positive control is that the same scan finds the +0x178C and +0x1788 writes three and six bytes earlier in the same instruction stream.

struct_fields.name: graphics
struct_fields.revises: The field is named session_sibling and says 'Not identified'. Two other records in the same file identify it - CGui +0x30's comment calls it the CGraphics by live pointer equality - and the construction chain below names it statically.
struct_fields.comment: The CEU3Graphics. Constructor argument 2, = CFrontEnd +0x20C = CBackEndIdler +0xB4. Returned by virtual slot 17. Statically: LoadEverything passes **CEU3Application +0x11C**, which project.json already names `graphics`, as CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd's arg2 at 0x2329D4/0x2329DC; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg2 at +0x20C; CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler copies [frontEnd+0x20C] to +0x178C at 0x248412. MakeBackEndIdler writes the same object to CBackEndIdler +0xB4 beside +0xB8 = the application, and ProcessSessionEndRequests hands (+0x178C, +0x60, +0x1790) back to CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd as (graphics, gui, app).
struct_fields.evidence: Same construction chain as +0x1790, one argument earlier: 0x648412 `mov [ebx+0x178c], edi` with edi = [ebp+0xC] = [frontEnd+0x20C]; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg2 there; LoadEverything passes [application+0x11C] as arg2 at 0x6329D4/0x6329DC, and +0x11C is already named `graphics` in project.json from a live RTTI read. Corroborated from a third direction by CGui +0x30's own comment, which says this is the same object as CInGameIdler +0x178C by live pointer equality. **What would show it wrong:** CEU3Application +0x11C not being the graphics - it was named live, and the static chain here does not re-establish it, so this entry inherits that entry's confidence rather than adding to it. If +0x11C were mis-named, this name is wrong in the same way and for the same reason.

struct_fields.name: session
struct_fields.comment: The CSession. CEU3Application::CEU3Application (0x22F080) builds the startup session with mode 2 at 0x22F30F and stores it here; CInGameIdler::GetSession (virtual slot 18, 0x24D800) is three instructions returning [this+0x1790]->[0x12C], and CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock tests +0x34 on the result and posts through +0x38. The class is `CSession` from the session.cpp strings its constructor 0x6887A0 carries ('NoAdress', 'InitialSession'); the field's own type is left void* because nothing here read the object's layout.
struct_fields.evidence: Two readers and one writer, all already in project.json's own comments: the constructor stores the startup session at [this+0x12C] (0x22F30F), and CInGameIdler::GetSession (0x24D800, virtual slot 18) is three instructions returning [[idler+0x1790]+0x12C]. The class name CSession comes from the constructor at rva 0x6887A0 (VA 0xA887A0), which project.json identifies from its session.cpp strings. **What would show it wrong:** the offset being read on something other than the application - but the only reader goes through +0x1790, which this same fragment establishes. The type is deliberately left void* because the object's layout was not read, so only the name is being claimed.

slots_noted: None of the four addresses is in any virtual table: mergeFindings.inTables() returns nothing for 0x67B240, 0x63A330, 0x62F080 or 0x6087C0, and image.findValue over .rdata finds none of them in a table entry. So no vftable_slots record is owed.
